name: David Shapiro
role: Writer and YouTuber; author of Labor Zero (2026)
why: Coined and develops Post-Labor Economics, the framing this wiki organises: the Great Decoupling, economic agency, the two pyramids and the Labor/Zero movement.

name: David Autor
why: Task-based theory of technology and work; why automation has not ended jobs so far; where new work comes from.

name: Daron Acemoglu and Pascual Restrepo
why: The displacement and reinstatement framework, and measured effects of industrial robots on US labour markets.

name: Erik Brynjolfsson
why: Field evidence on generative AI at work and early payroll evidence on AI-exposed young workers.

name: Anton Korinek
why: Macroeconomic scenarios for a transition to artificial general intelligence, including ones where wages collapse.

name: Aaron Benanav
why: The strongest critique of automation explanations: weak labour demand comes from slow growth, not fast robots.

name: Philippe Van Parijs
why: The philosophical case for an unconditional basic income as real freedom for all.

name: Hilary Hoynes and Jesse Rothstein
why: The sharpest cost-based critique of UBI in rich countries: universal payments large enough to help the poor would be enormously expensive.

name: Thomas Piketty
why: Long-run data on capital and its returns, the backdrop for ownership-based income.

name: Darrick Hamilton and William Darity Jr.
role: Economists, The New School and Duke
why: Designed baby bonds: publicly funded trust accounts at birth, larger for poorer families.

name: Yanis Varoufakis
why: Argues platform capital has already turned markets into fiefdoms: technofeudalism.

name: GiveDirectly
role: Charity running cash transfers, including the 12-year Kenya UBI study
why: Delivers the transfers studied in several of the best-known cash experiments.

name: OpenResearch
why: Ran the three-year, $1,000-a-month unconditional cash study in Texas and Illinois.

name: Stanford Basic Income Lab
why: Tracks guaranteed-income pilots and their evaluations across the US.

name: Alaska Permanent Fund Corporation
why: The fund behind the only universal, permanent citizen dividend in the US.

name: Norges Bank Investment Management
role: Manages Norway's Government Pension Fund Global
why: The world's largest sovereign wealth fund, owned by citizens through the state budget rather than a dividend.

name: International Labour Organization
why: Global labour income share estimates and the generative-AI exposure index.
